name: SmoothCursor
description: A soft dot or ring that trails the real pointer with easing, inside a container or across the page. The system cursor stays unless you ask to hide it.

children.description: Content of the container. With scope "page" the children are rendered as they are and the follower covers the whole window.

scope.description: Where the follower lives: inside the wrapper around the children, or over the whole window.

shape.description: A filled dot or an open ring.

color.description: Any CSS colour. Defaults to the primary action colour.

smoothing.description: How quickly the follower catches up, from 0.02 (lazy) to 1 (no lag).

hideNativeCursor.description: Hides the system pointer over the container once a mouse is in use. Off by default: keep it off unless the follower is clearly visible everywhere.

isStill.description: Switches the follower off and leaves the system pointer alone.

requirements: Decoration for mouse users: the follower is aria-hidden, ignores the pointer (pointer-events none) and never takes focus
It never replaces keyboard focus: focus rings are untouched and nothing depends on where the follower is
Not shown for touch or pen input, for prefers-reduced-motion, with isStill, or inside rdm-still
The system pointer is only hidden when hideNativeCursor is set, and only after a mouse has moved over the container
The frame loop runs only while the follower is catching up and stops when it arrives; listeners are removed on unmount
Forced-colors: the follower keeps its own colour (forced-color-adjust none) so it stays visible
screenReader: Not announced: the follower is purely visual

use_when: A playful hero or showcase area for mouse users
A soft highlight that follows the pointer over a canvas or gallery
avoid_when: Forms, dashboards and anywhere precise pointing matters
Anything that would be unusable without the follower
anti_patterns: Hiding the system pointer over text fields and small controls
Using it as the only hover feedback
Very large or fully opaque followers that cover what is being pointed at
